$comment: Guided lessons (Studio → Lessons). Each step lights `controls` on the drawing, switches the Visualizer to `view` and, with a `goal`, advances by itself once the S-1 (or the drawing) reports the knob moves: every `when` condition holds (CC value min/max, 0–127) and at least `moves` CC messages for the `touch` CCs (default: the `when` CCs) arrived during the step. Steps without a goal have a Next button. `cite` is a verbatim quote from that page of the S-1 manual (checked by `npm run validate:lessons`). `setup` holds knob CCs sent by 'Set up the lesson', on top of baseSetup.

lessons.title: Oscillators and waveforms
lessons.blurb: Saw and square: the raw material of every S-1 sound.

steps.title: Start with a sawtooth
steps.do: Hold a note (or press Hold A2), then turn the SAW level up until it’s nearly full.
steps.listen: Bright and buzzy, like brass or bowed strings.
steps.look: A ramp that climbs, then drops straight down once per cycle.

cite.quote: The wave includes the nth harmonic at a volume of 1/n, with the fundamental wave considered as “1”.

steps.title: Swap to the square
steps.do: Turn SAW all the way down and SQUARE up.
steps.listen: Hollow and woody, like a clarinet.
steps.look: Flat tops and bottoms joined by straight edges.

cite.quote: However, the even-numbered harmonics are left out entirely.

steps.title: Blend them and see the harmonics
steps.do: Keep SQUARE up and bring SAW back up too, watching the spectrum.
steps.listen: Thicker than either wave on its own.
steps.look: The square has only odd harmonics (1×, 3×, 5× the note); the saw fills in the even ones between them.

cite.quote: Square waves are composed of a fundamental sine wave and the sine waves of the odd-numbered harmonics, all at a fixed ratio.

steps.title: Change the octave
steps.do: Turn RANGE a couple of clicks either way.
steps.listen: The same sound, an octave lower or higher per click.
steps.look: The pitch readout jumps by octaves while the wave keeps its shape.

cite.quote: By switching the settings from 64′ all the way down to 2′, you can change the tonal range in octaves.

lessons.title: Sub oscillator and noise
lessons.blurb: Add weight underneath, or hiss with no pitch at all.

steps.title: Add the sub oscillator
steps.do: With the saw playing, turn SUB up.
steps.listen: More weight underneath: a square wave an octave or two below.
steps.look: The pitch readout drops an octave and the wave repeats half as often.

cite.quote: Adjusts the level of the sub oscillator.

steps.title: Pick the sub’s octave
steps.do: Hold SHIFT and press the SUB OCT key, then turn TEMPO/VALUE: -1oc, -2oc or -2o.A.
steps.listen: -2oc sits two octaves down; -2o.A is a thinner, asymmetrical version.
steps.look: At -2oc each cycle is twice as long again.

cite.quote: Hold down the [SHIFT] button and press the [SUB OCT] pad.

steps.title: Noise
steps.do: Turn SAW and SUB down and NOISE up. (If NOISE plays a rising riser instead, Riser Mode is on: switch it OFF in the menu.)
steps.listen: A hiss with no pitch, the stuff of wind, snares and sweeps.
steps.look: The spectrum fills from bottom to top with no harmonic peaks, and the scope can’t find a pitch.

cite.quote: Adjusts the level of the noise.

steps.title: Pink or white
steps.do: Hold SHIFT and turn NOISE to switch between pink and white noise.
steps.listen: White noise is brighter; pink noise is darker and softer.
steps.look: White noise puts more energy in the highs.

cite.quote: NOISE MODE ([SHIFT] button + pad [15] (MENU): Noise Mode) ([SHIFT] + OSCILLATOR [NOISE] knob)

lessons.title: Filter and resonance
lessons.blurb: Carve the harmonics away and make the cutoff sing.

steps.title: Close the filter
steps.do: Hold a note and slowly turn FREQ down to about a third.
steps.listen: Darker and softer as the highs disappear.
steps.look: The saw’s sharp edge rounds off towards a sine wave.

cite.quote: Turning the knob counterclockwise cuts the higher frequencies and makes the waveform closer to that of a sine wave.

steps.title: Watch the harmonics come back
steps.do: Turn FREQ back up while watching the spectrum.
steps.listen: The brightness returns.
steps.look: Harmonics above the cutoff fall away; the low ones always pass.

cite.quote: This lets you pass the lower frequencies through while cutting the higher frequencies (LPF: Low-Pass Filter).

steps.title: Add resonance
steps.do: Set FREQ to about halfway, then turn RESO up.
steps.listen: A nasal, whistling edge.
steps.look: A peak appears at the cutoff; on the scope, ripples ring after each edge.

cite.quote: Emphasizes the frequencies around the cutoff point that you set using the [FREQ] knob.

steps.title: The classic sweep
steps.do: Keep RESO up and sweep FREQ slowly all the way up.
steps.listen: The famous synth sweep: the resonant peak sings as it rises.
steps.look: The peak draws a bright rising line in the spectrogram.

cite.quote: In particular, when you move the cutoff point while the resonance is raised, you can get a sound that’s unique to synthesizers.

lessons.title: Envelopes (ADSR)
lessons.blurb: Shape every note over time: swells, plucks and tails.

steps.title: Attack
steps.do: Turn ATTACK up past halfway and play a few notes on the pads.
steps.listen: Each note fades in instead of starting at once.
steps.look: Notes start dim and brighten in the spectrogram.

cite.quote: This knob sets the time (attack time) it takes for the control signal to reach its peak level after you press a keyboard pad.

steps.title: Decay and sustain: a pluck
steps.do: Turn ATTACK and SUSTAIN down, set DECAY to about a third, and play short notes.
steps.listen: A pluck: loud at first, then gone even while you hold the pad.
steps.look: Short bright blips that fade quickly.

cite.quote: This knob sets the sustain level, which is the level that the sound stays at after the envelope reaches its peak.

steps.title: Release
steps.do: Bring SUSTAIN back up and turn RELEASE up.
steps.listen: Notes ring on after you let go of the pad.
steps.look: Each note trails off after its pad is released.

cite.quote: This knob sets the time (release time) it takes for the control signal to drop to zero (where the envelope reaches its end) after you release the keyboard pad.

steps.title: The envelope on the filter
steps.do: Turn FREQ down to about halfway, turn the filter ENV knob up, and play short notes.
steps.listen: A “wow” at the start of every note as the filter opens and closes.
steps.look: Harmonics flare up at each note’s start, then fall back.

cite.quote: Use this to make changes in the sound over a short time within single notes.

lessons.title: LFO: movement
lessons.blurb: Vibrato, wobble and random steps from the low-frequency oscillator.

steps.title: Vibrato
steps.do: Hold a note and turn the OSCILLATOR LFO knob up a little.
steps.listen: The pitch wobbles.
steps.look: The harmonic lines wave up and down together.

cite.quote: This knob adjusts the modulation intensity, when you use the modulator signal from the LFO section to control the fundamental frequency (pitch) of the OSC.

steps.title: Speed
steps.do: Turn RATE to slow the wobble down and speed it up.
steps.listen: From a slow sway to a fast flutter.
steps.look: The waves in the spectrogram stretch out or bunch up.

cite.quote: This knob sets the LFO and RANDOM speed (frequency).

steps.title: Shape
steps.do: Turn WAVE FORM through the LFO shapes, including RND (random).
steps.listen: Smooth sweeps, jumps between two pitches, random steps.
steps.look: The lines change from curves to steps.

cite.quote: With the RND (RANDOM) setting, the unit outputs a control signal that changes randomly, which is used to produce random notes (OSC) or random filter (FILTER) effects.

steps.title: Wah with the filter LFO
steps.do: Turn the OSCILLATOR LFO back down and the FILTER LFO up. A lower FREQ makes it stronger.
steps.listen: A wah or growl instead of a pitch wobble.
steps.look: The upper harmonics pulse while the pitch stays put.

cite.quote: This adjusts the intensity (depth) when controlling the filter’s cutoff point with the modulator signal from the LFO section.

lessons.title: Chords and arpeggios
lessons.blurb: Poly mode, one-finger chords and the arpeggiator.

steps.title: Poly mode
steps.do: Hold SHIFT, press POLY and turn TEMPO/VALUE to PoLy. Then play a chord on the pads.
steps.listen: Up to four notes at once.
steps.look: Several sets of harmonics stack up in the spectrum.

cite.quote: Lets you play more than one tone at the same time (up to four voices).

steps.title: One-finger chords
steps.do: Keep turning TEMPO/VALUE to Chd, then press pad 2 (ENTER) to switch voices 2–4 on and shift their keys. Now one pad plays a chord.
steps.listen: A full chord from a single finger.
steps.look: One pad, several stacks of harmonics.

cite.quote: Plays voices 2–4 at the same time for each note that you play, according to the parameter settings below.

steps.title: Turn the arpeggiator on
steps.do: Hold SHIFT and press pad 8 (ARPEGGIO ON) to switch it on, then hold a few pads together.
steps.listen: Your chord plays one note at a time, over and over.
steps.look: A staircase of notes in the spectrogram.

cite.quote: On the S-1, you can automatically arpeggiate the chords you play on the keyboard pad.

steps.title: Arp type and latch
steps.do: SHIFT + pad 9 (ARPEGGIO TYPE) picks Up, Down, Random and more. Press HOLD while it plays to keep it going hands-free.
steps.listen: The same notes in a new order.
steps.look: The staircase changes direction or scatters.

cite.quote: When you press the [HOLD] button to make it light up while an arpeggio is playing, the arpeggio keeps playing even after you take your finger off the keyboard pad.

lessons.title: Delay and reverb
lessons.blurb: Echoes and space around short notes.

steps.title: Delay
steps.do: Play short notes and turn DELAY up.
steps.listen: Echoes repeat after each note.
steps.look: Each note leaves a trail of fading copies.

cite.quote: This adds an echoing effect by delaying the sound and repeating the delay.

steps.title: Delay time
steps.do: Hold SHIFT and turn DELAY to change the time between echoes.
steps.listen: Slapback, rhythmic echoes or long gaps.
steps.look: The copies spread apart or bunch together.

cite.quote: You can set the delay time by turning the [DELAY] knob while holding down the [SHIFT] button.

steps.title: Reverb
steps.do: Turn DELAY back down and REVERB up.
steps.listen: A room or hall around the notes.
steps.look: A soft, smeared tail instead of separate copies.

cite.quote: This effect produces reverberation, like being in a hall or room.

steps.title: Reverb time
steps.do: Hold SHIFT and turn REVERB to make the space shorter or longer.
steps.listen: From a small room to a huge hall.
steps.look: The tail gets shorter or longer.

cite.quote: Adjust the reverb length (time) by turning the [REVERB] knob while holding down the [SHIFT] button.
